top_story: By 4 July, Tehran had turned Ali Khamenei’s week-long funeral rites into a mass display of regime endurance, building on gatherings that began the previous day and drawing officials, foreign dignitaries, and large crowds into the capital. The ceremonies project continuity after the killing of Iran’s central political arbiter, but they also open a sensitive succession period in which elite cohesion will matter as much as public choreography. That uncertainty lands in a region already shaped by acute civilian harm, including Israel’s 25 June strike on tents sheltering displaced Palestinians on a Gaza beach, where people already pushed by siege and hunger faced another lethal shock. The immediate picture is of an Islamic Republic trying to convert mourning into authority while regional publics absorb yet another reminder that power struggles are being lived most directly through insecurity, displacement, and loss.
